overview: Supervise one bounded extraction: correct its proposed scope, execute the approved saved revision and verify all five required values against the assigned source. Field counts, extra fields and XP do not replace these required outcomes.
instructions: Use Set Up Lab to add the assigned NSF Alpine Ecology proposal. Open the source and confirm its identity, readable text and saved lab workspace before preparing any extraction.

Use chat or the editor to create an extraction with PI Name, Institution, Total Budget, Project Period and Sponsoring Agency. Inspect the saved field meanings and selected document. Ask for a proposal and a stop before execution while you review.

Choose your saved extraction in Prepare a practical run. The training proposal deliberately names an unrelated source. Compare the proposed source with the NSF task, select the assigned source and explain your correction in your own words.

Review the captured source, workspace and fields before approving this saved scope. Approval records your decision; use the separate execution action to run it. If the reply is uncertain, inspect the saved run status before requesting another run.

Inspect the actual saved result. Record and check all five required values against the saved assigned source, including the full project budget and project period. Cite the supporting passage for each value; a quality score or fluent answer does not establish correctness.
If a required value or scope is wrong, correct the extraction and prepare a new run. Keep the original evidence and review history. Do not label unresolved values as verified.

Save your source checks before requesting automatic assessment of that exact work. Read its outcome-specific feedback and revise as needed. A technical grading failure preserves your work and is not a failed learner attempt. Draft feedback does not award module credit.
